questions.q: What does verifying a contract on a block explorer actually publish?
options: Only the contract's deployment transaction hash
The Solidity source, the exact compiler version/settings, and any constructor arguments — matched byte-for-byte against the deployed bytecode
A new copy of the contract on a different address
The deployer's private key, for transparency
questions.explain: Verification publishes source + compiler settings + constructor args, and the explorer recompiles and matches it exactly against the deployed bytecode.

questions.q: What becomes available on a contract's explorer page only after verification succeeds?
options: The ability to deploy a new version
The Read Contract and Write Contract tabs, plus decoded function calls and events instead of raw hex
A lower gas price for future transactions
Automatic bug bounty enrollment
questions.explain: Before verification, a contract is opaque bytecode; after a successful match, the explorer unlocks Read/Write tabs and decodes calls and events using the published ABI.

questions.q: What does `cast abi-encode` produce, and why does `forge verify-contract` need it for `--constructor-args`?
options: A random nonce for the transaction
The exact ABI encoding of the constructor arguments as they were actually passed at deploy time — a mismatch fails the bytecode match
The contract's compiled bytecode
A list of all function selectors
questions.explain: Verification requires the constructor arguments ABI-encoded exactly as deployed — cast abi-encode produces that precise encoding, and even a correct-looking but misformatted value fails verification.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the Advanced Configuration section (Optimization, Runs, EVM Version) is where verification most often fails on an otherwise-correct contract?
options: Because those fields are optional and can be left blank
Because those settings have to match the actual values used at compile/deploy time exactly, not reasonable-looking defaults
Because Etherscan ignores those fields entirely
Because those fields only matter for proxy contracts
questions.explain: If Optimization, Runs, or EVM Version don't match what was actually used to compile and deploy the contract, the recompiled bytecode won't match, and verification fails even though the source is correct.

questions.q: What does a successful Etherscan verification result expose, according to the lesson's screenshot?
options: Only a green checkmark with no further detail
Compiler version, optimization settings, and the generated Contract ABI
The deployer's full transaction history
A list of other contracts deployed by the same address
questions.explain: The verification success screen shown in this lesson displays the compiler version, optimization settings, and the Contract ABI/bytecode, now readable instead of opaque.
